description: Steady-state 2D slab-on-grade heat transfer problem inspired by BESTEST-GC (ASHRAE Standard 140). Compute floor heat loss per unit length (W/m) for a strip foundation cross-section.

domain.description: 2D vertical cross-section from building centerline (x=0, symmetry axis) to far field. y-axis points downward from the ground surface. The slab and foundation wall form a continuous concrete structure at the surface.

components.slab: Concrete slab from x=0 to x=slab_half_width, y=0 to y=slab_thickness
components.foundation_wall: Concrete perimeter wall from x=slab_half_width to x=slab_half_width+wall_width, y=0 to y=slab_thickness. Same material as slab. Separates indoor slab surface from outdoor ground surface.
components.insulation: Optional insulation layer directly beneath the slab (not under wall)
components.soil: Fills the remainder of the computational domain

boundary_conditions.top_slab_surface: T = T_indoor_C (Dirichlet, y=0, x in [0, slab_half_width])
boundary_conditions.top_wall: dT/dy = 0 (adiabatic Neumann, y=0, x in (slab_half_width, slab_half_width + wall_width])
boundary_conditions.top_ground_surface: T = T_outdoor_C (Dirichlet, y=0, x > slab_half_width + wall_width)

foundation_wall.description: Concrete perimeter wall extending beyond the slab edge at the same depth as the slab. Its top surface is adiabatic (below-grade, no direct heat exchange with air). Material properties are identical to the slab.

governing_equation: Steady-state heat conduction: div(k * grad(T)) = 0, where k is the local thermal conductivity. Use harmonic mean of adjacent cell conductivities at material interfaces.

output.description: Total 2D floor heat loss per unit length for the full slab width (accounting for symmetry), in W/m. This is the downward heat flux integrated over the indoor slab surface at y=0 from x=0 to x=slab_half_width, multiplied by 2 for symmetry.
output.format: JSON object at /app/results.json with case names as keys and numeric heat loss values (W/m) as values
